# Local English demonstration audio

230 mono 16-bit PCM WAV files: 48 teaching symbols, 26 letter names, one
alphabet and 40 lesson recordings for each of two synthetic British voices.
Playback is offline; the browser receives WAV files, not a speech model.
These are synthetic demonstrations, not human recordings.

## Letter names and connected speech (114 files)

`interactive-lab/build.sh natural` runs `generate-natural-audio.py`
with Kokoro v1.0, kokoro-onnx 0.6.1 and the British voices bf_emma / bm_george.
Generation speed is 0.9; no reverb, echo or post-generation time stretching
is applied. Files are resampled to 22050 Hz mono PCM with short silent margins.
Alphabet intervals correspond exactly to the individual letter recordings.

The script verifies model checksums and stages all output before replacing
assets. The manifests record each file's engine, voice, duration and SHA256.
Word boundaries use the model duration output. Within-word phoneme poses
are proportional teaching guides, not measured phoneme or forced alignment.
Short utterance quality and accent still require a teacher's listening review.

Kokoro model (Apache-2.0): https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M
ONNX export and wrapper (MIT): https://github.com/thewh1teagle/kokoro-onnx
Fixed model/voice release: https://github.com/thewh1teagle/kokoro-onnx/releases/tag/model-files-v1.1

## Isolated phonemes (116 files including lesson sounds)

Generated by `generate-audio.py` and `generate-curriculum-audio.py` using
eSpeak NG via espeakng-loader 0.2.4, with en+f3 / en+m3 configurations.
Explicit phoneme inputs prevent a sound such as /d/ being read as “dee”.
These retain the formant-synthesized timbre; replacing them with unverified
short neural outputs could change the phoneme being taught.

Full vowels use citation stress (schwa stays unstressed). Long monophthongs
use synthesis rate 95 and short ones 170 to emphasize the teaching contrast.
Distinct phoneme inputs are used; no repetition or pitch shifting creates
long/short pairs. This duration contrast is not a fixed natural-speech ratio.

Source (GPL-3.0-or-later): https://github.com/espeak-ng/espeak-ng
The engine is a build dependency and is not shipped in this web app.
Anatomical model attribution is separate in `../ATTRIBUTION.md`.

At runtime 1× means the original file speed. User-selected slow playback
preserves pitch but can still introduce browser time-stretch artifacts.
Audio-clock synchronization does not certify anatomical or pronunciation accuracy.

Isolated phonemes use gain only to raise quiet peaks to -6 dBFS, retaining
the original samples' timing and silence. Louder recordings are unchanged.
Run `bash build.sh volume` from `interactive-lab` to normalize existing
phonemes, synchronize course sound recordings, and update manifest hashes.
This operation is idempotent and does not regenerate neural speech.
